1  HON'BLE JITENDRA KUMAR SINHA, J. 
1.
Heard Shri H.R. Mishra, learned Senior Advocate assisted by Shri S.P. Vishwakarma, learned counsel for the applicant, Shri B.P. Maurya, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime no.207 of 2025,
under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471 of I.P.C., Police Station Bansi, District Siddharth Nagar, with the prayer that in the event of arrest, applicant may be released on bail.
3. It has been argued by the learned Senior Advocate that applicant is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
It is further submitted that the first information report has been lodged by the Settlement Officer of Consolidation after deciding the appeal.
It is further submitted that the applicant is not the beneficiary of the alleged transaction.
It is further submitted that as per allegation, the applicant is said to have obtained an order of entry in favour his daughter in the revenue records (Khatauni) by playing fraud with the Court.

It is further submitted that the applicant has already filed two revisions before the revisional Court against the order of Settlement Officer of Consolidation, which is still pending and the matter is still subjudice.
It is further submitted that the applicant is having criminal history, which has been explained in the memo of application.
It was also submitted that applicant undertakes to co-operate during trial and he would appear as and when required by the investigating agency or Court.

It has been stated that in case,
applicant is granted anticipatory bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail and will co-operate with the investigation and would obey all conditions of bail.
4. On the other hand, learned A.G.A. has opposed the application for anticipatory bail.

5. As per first information report, the applicant is said to have obtained an order from the revenue Court by playing fraud, thereby getting the name of his daughter registered in the revenue records (Khatauni).

The first information report has been filed by the appellate authority i.e. the Settlement Officer of Consolidation, against which, two revisions were filed, which is still pending and the matter is still subjudice.
It is further submitted that the applicant is having criminal history, which has been explained in the memo of application.

6. It may be stated that in case of Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra, (2011) 1 SCC 694, it has been held by Hon'ble Supreme Court that while deciding anticipatory bail, Court must consider nature and gravity of accusation, antecedent of accused, possibility of accused to flee from justice and that Court must evaluate entire available material against the accused carefully and that the exact role of the accused has also to be taken into consideration.

submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, role of applicant and all attending facts and circumstances of the case, without expressing any opinion on merits, a case for anticipatory bail is made out.

2 8. The anticipatory bail application is allowed.
9. In the event of arrest of the applicant- Fazlurrahman involved in the aforesaid case crime shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 50,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned, till submission of police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C. / 193(3) BNSS with the following conditions :-
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence and that he would appear before the trial Court on the date fixed unless exempted by the Court concerned;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him/her/them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(iii) The applicant would co-
operate during trial and would not misuse the liberty of bail.
(iv) The applicant shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court concerned.
10. In default of any of the conditions, the prosecution shall be at liberty to file appropriate application for cancellation of anticipatory bail granted to the applicant.
